_what: WHICH TENANTS ARE IN SCOPE for import/audit reporting, and which are deliberately excluded -- with a reason, per tenant.
_why: Rob, 2026-09-11: 'amyblair and onscene as well as a bunch of the others will be excluded at some point so we likely won't need to account for them or only account for them seperatlye'
Without this, every report re-surfaces tenants we have already decided not to care about, and the real queue is buried in noise. With it, the queue is short and the exclusions are auditable.
_rules: EXCLUSION IS NOT DELETION. An excluded tenant is reported in its OWN section with its reason, never silently dropped. Every count prints IN-SCOPE and EXCLUDED side by side, because a number with a hidden denominator is how a finding disappears without anyone deciding it should.

EVERY EXCLUSION CARRIES A REASON AND A DATE. A reason-less exclusion is indistinguishable from a mistake, and this repo already learned that from registry rows that suppressed findings while reading like completed adjudications.
deptId IS THE KEY. Subdomains get renamed; the subdomain field here is a convenience label for humans and is NOT what matching uses.
`revisit: true` means the decision is expected to change (a tenant being migrated, a hold that will lift). `revisit: false` means it is settled (a demo tenant nobody supports). Both stay listed.
NOTHING IS EXCLUDED UNTIL ROB SAYS SO. The candidates below are a PROPOSAL derived from measurement; they are NOT applied and must not be treated as decisions.
source: tools/config/tenant_scope.json -- hand-maintained, consumed by the import-plan and audit reports

_candidates._status: PROPOSAL ONLY -- NOT APPLIED. Nothing in this block affects any report. Move an entry into `excluded` to apply it.
_candidates._how_derived: From the 2026-09-11 content measurement of all 64 carrier tenants plus the 1785-row roster. Grouped by the REASON they would be excluded, because the reason decides whether it is settled or revisitable.

not_our_build._what:
Carries a provider bundle with NO 'Provider configuration for

vX.Y' description -- confirmed by CONTENT to match no build in our history. We did not build these and do not version them.
not_our_build.note: Includes the 24-tenant LA_LEMS demo family (4 byte-identical configs copied across many tenants), Lafayette Parish (ledger already records it as hand-built by engineering), sdso/sandiegoso-foundation, gordo, ccpd, and usx-fl-fcic (Rob ruled that an unrelated test on 2026-09-10).

third_party_or_unowned._what: Runs OUR build but is not a tenant we track or support. These are the two Rob named.

qa_and_practice._what: QA / practice / demo tenants that run our build but are not deployments anyone is accountable for.

held_by_decision._what: Genuinely behind, and DELIBERATELY so -- the ledger already records the decision. These should be reported separately rather than excluded, so the hold stays visible and does not quietly become a forgotten gap.
held_by_decision.recommendation: HOLD, do not EXCLUDE. A hold that stops being reported is how a stale LIVE tenant becomes invisible -- and hawaii-dle is LIVE.

deactivated._what: Status DEACTIVATED in the department index -- cannot serve queries. Rob: 'we can filter out deavtivated tenants'.
deactivated.note: This is a STATUS filter, not a per-tenant decision, so it belongs in the tools as a switch rather than as 225 rows here. All 64 known carriers are non-deactivated, so filtering costs nothing in coverage.
